title: Atletico Madrid in talks over move for Juventus striker Jonathan David
content:
Atletico Madrid are in talks over a move for Juventus striker Jonathan David.

Previously, Atletico had monitored a deal for Nicolas Jackson, but the striker has since joined Aston Villa from Chelsea. Atletico are now trying to bring in David on a season-long loan.

Sources, speaking on the condition of anonymity so they could do so candidly, indicated a move for the 26-year-old Canada international go ahead, David’s arrival would be to increase the club’s depth at centre-forward rather than replace any of the strikers already at the club.

Nevertheless, Julian Alvarez’s situation remains one to watch, with Arsenal and Barcelona maintaining an interest in the forward. Atletico have made it clear in recent days with multiple public statements that they do not wish to sell the Argentina international to the Catalan club.

David had a disappointing debut campaign with Juventus, scoring six league goals, after joining the Turin club on a free transfer from Lille last summer.

He had previously enjoyed a successful five-year spell with French club Lille, which saw him hit double figures in the Ligue 1 goalscoring charts in each of his seasons with the club.

The Canada international was a prominent figure for his country as it co-hosted this summer’s World Cup. He scored three goals in his five appearances, though they all came in the 6-0 group-stage win against Qatar.

His contract at Juventus runs through to 2030.

David joined Lille from Belgian side Gent in 2020 in a record deal for the French club, and scored 19 goals in his debut season as his side lifted the Ligue 1 title for the first time since 2011. The forward registered 109 goals in 232 appearances for Lille, putting him second in the club’s all-time top scorers list.

He notched 25 or more goals in each of his final three seasons at Lille, including some important contributions in the Champions League, including the winner in a 1-0 victory against Real Madrid, and a brace in a 3-1 win against Atletico Madrid during his final season at the club.

Chelsea held talks with David’s representatives in June 2024, but did not proceed with a move.
